non_blocking_findings: The test scan is one level deep: 'grep -oHE ... tests/*.gd' never sees a test script in a tests/ subdirectory (my MU4). No such file exists today (tests/ holds only fixtures and data below its top level), so nothing is broken today, but a future test placed in tests/<dir>/ would be invisible to the guard. A recursive scan or an explicit 'no test scripts below tests/*/' assertion would close it.

The scan is anchored on the literal 'journey_sim.', so a feature test that compares the same session's minor through another variable name is invisible (my MU3). The design's Risks name the 'a local variable' form, but the anchor turns the miss into silence rather than a rejection.

A constant-first comparison ('SimBridge.EARTH_LOG_MINOR == journey_sim.want_minor') is not scanned (my MU2). This is exactly the design's Follow-up F4, already recorded as non-blocking by the round-2 reviewers; the scan's ok line still reports '4 test comparisons name it', which can read as complete coverage when it is not.

The guard accepts a DOWNGRADE of SESSION_MINOR to any defined protocol minor (my MU9, 18 -> 17). This is inside the approved non-goal (b''), but the fast tier cannot tell an upgrade from a downgrade, so a downgrade merges green and is caught only by the nightly comms-station floor (I measured it: 'comms-station: 41 passed, 1 failures'). Worth stating in the doc's Risks, which cover a duplicate value but not a downgrade.

The guard is lexical by construction: a write the text does not show (a helper, my MU1) passes the fast tier. I confirmed the documented mitigation end to end - on the mutated tree the guard says 'ok' while the nightly loading-jump check says 'FAIL map: the map's simulation is the prefetched one' (76 passed, 1 failure). The split is as designed; this is the note that it holds.

The controls' 'orphan' case hard-codes the value 99 ('const SESSION_MINOR := 99'). If a protocol minor ever reaches 99 that control's premise becomes false. Same class as the 7AH finding about a literal-pinned ERE; it fails loudly, not silently.

The design doc's Conflict-surface prose says the Makefile merges with origin/feat/r2-kerr-table-preflight and origin/feat/r2-kerr with 0 conflicts. My git merge-file measurement gives conflicts=1 for both. The conflict is the pre-existing 'AILANG_RELEASE ?= v0.56.0' vs 'v0.56.1' line, it reproduces identically with origin/main's Makefile alone (so it is not caused by this row), and a whole-tree git merge-tree shows the Makefile auto-merging with the only conflict in tools/python-allowlist.txt (also pre-existing). The doc's claim is stale, not the implementation.
The design header says the control script is 183 lines; revision 2's three extra cases make it 204 (the sprint scope says 204 and the committed file is 204). Cosmetic staleness in the doc's header.
